newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul won ends lower, import settlement scheduled.
newsitem.headline: Seoul won ends lower, import settlement scheduled.

text.p: The won closed slightly lower against the dollar in narrow trading on Thursday as market players prepared for scheduled import settlements, traders said.
The won ended at 843.90, against the opening price of 843.60. It touched a high of 843.40, and fears of central bank intervention kept the won from falling below a low of 844.00.
"Most dealers expect intervention over the 844 figure, but because of import settlments, there's a need for more dollars in the market," said a European bank dealer.
He estimated about $500 million worth of settlements had to be met between Friday and Tuesday.
A local bank dealer said he expected similar narrow band trading on Friday, with the won/dollar range moving between 843 and 844.
The European bank dealer said he expected the won to fall further, moving between 844 and 847.
The central bank set Friday's base mid-rate at 843.80, compared to Thursday's 843.70.
